title: The form that wasn't broken
teaser: An invitation went out. The sign-up form was closed. Marketing wants to know who took it offline.
misunderstanding: Marketing understood the 10:00 launch as unconditional; the agreed opening depended on Legal's approval.

email.subject: Why was the sign-up form taken offline?
email.body:
Hi Daniel,

We confirmed yesterday that sign-ups would open at 10. The invitation has gone out, but Support is sending me screenshots of a closed form. Why did Product take it offline without telling us? We may need to email the whole list again, and I need an explanation before the 1pm campaign review.

Maya

document.title: Launch handover · campaign notes
document.intro: These notes were available internally before Maya wrote. They are the only confirmed facts you can rely on.

facts.text: The team agreed to open sign-ups Tuesday at 10:00, provided Legal approved the final privacy wording.
The campaign calendar scheduled the invitation for 10:00 but did not include the Legal approval condition.
Legal requested a wording change. Daniel posted the delay in the Product channel, not the shared campaign channel.
The invitation was sent. The form had not opened yet; it displayed 'Registration opens soon'.
Legal approved the wording at 10:23. The form opened at 10:31.
Support forwarded three screenshots. The total number of people who tried to register while the form was closed is unknown.

questions.prompt: Which statement in Maya's email goes beyond the confirmed facts?

options.text: The invitation has already been sent.
options.feedback: The campaign notes confirm it was sent at 10:00.

options.text: Product took an open form offline.
options.feedback: The form was never open before 10:31. Maya's wording assumes it had been live.

options.text: Support sent screenshots of a closed form.
options.feedback: Support did forward three screenshots.

questions.prompt: What was the actual condition for opening sign-ups?

options.text: Marketing had to send the invitation first.
options.feedback: The invitation was scheduled, but it was not the condition for opening.

options.text: Support had to test every registration.
options.feedback: The notes do not assign Support that condition.

options.text: Legal had to approve the privacy wording.
options.feedback: Monday's agreement made Legal approval a condition of the 10:00 opening.

questions.prompt: What does Maya need from Daniel before the review?

options.text: A reliable timeline and a plan for checking the impact.
options.feedback: She needs an explanation and a decision about a possible correction.

options.text: Proof that Marketing caused the problem.
options.feedback: Blame will not establish the impact or help decide what to tell recipients.

options.text: A promise that only three people were affected.
options.feedback: Three screenshots are reports, not the total number of affected people.

questions.prompt: Which response would clarify the situation without shifting blame?

options.text: Say Marketing ignored the checklist and must fix the email alone.
options.feedback: The calendar omitted the condition, but Daniel also missed the shared update.

options.text: Explain the condition, own the missed update, and propose an impact check.
options.feedback: This addresses the misunderstanding, Daniel's part, and Maya's next decision.

options.text: Apologise for taking the live form offline and promise a full resend.
options.feedback: The form was not taken offline, and a full resend has not been justified.

task.prompt: Reply to Maya as Daniel. Clarify what happened, acknowledge the communication gap you caused, distinguish confirmed reports from the unknown total impact, and propose a decision before the 1pm review.
criteria: Correct the assumption without blaming Maya
Separate three screenshots from total impact
Offer a concrete check and decision

model.subject: Re: Why was the sign-up form taken offline?
model.body:
Hi Maya,

I'm sorry the invitation went out while registration was still closed. The form was not taken offline after launch: it had not opened yet because the final privacy wording was awaiting Legal approval. That condition was in Monday's launch agreement, but I should have flagged the delay in the shared campaign channel when Legal requested a change at 9:42. I only posted in Product, which left your team without the information it needed.

Legal approved the wording at 10:23, and the form opened at 10:31. Support has forwarded three screenshots; we do not yet know how many people tried to register during that half hour. I'll check what we can confirm from the sign-up records and Support reports. Could we decide together, before the 1pm review, whether to contact affected people or send a wider correction?

Daniel

annotations.label: Takes responsibility
annotations.excerpt: I should have flagged the delay

annotations.label: Preserves uncertainty
annotations.excerpt: we do not yet know how many people

title: Done for whom?
teaser: A ticket says Done. A client cannot find the feature on her phone. Is the release broken?
misunderstanding: The ticket covered desktop export; an unqualified handover made the completion sound broader.

email.subject: Brookline can't find Export
email.body:
Hi Omar,

Nia at Brookline opened Reports on her phone during our call and found no Export button. I told her export was ready because the ticket is marked Done. Did we ship a broken release? I need a clear explanation for tomorrow's client check-in.

Lena

document.title: Ticket P-248 · handover record
document.intro: Read the scope and handover before deciding what Omar can safely say.

facts.text: P-248 says: 'Add CSV export to the desktop Reports page.' Mobile export is explicitly outside this ticket and remains in the backlog.
QA passed the desktop CSV export flow.
Omar marked P-248 Done and wrote 'Export is ready' in the handover without specifying desktop.
Nia's screenshot shows the mobile Reports page. There is no evidence that desktop export is broken.
No delivery date for mobile export has been agreed.

questions.prompt: What does the Done status actually verify?

options.text: Desktop CSV export is complete and passed QA.
options.feedback: That is the ticket's scope and the flow QA tested.

options.text: Every export flow is available.
options.feedback: The ticket names only the desktop Reports page.

options.text: Mobile export is ready for Brookline.
options.feedback: Mobile export is outside this ticket and still in the backlog.

questions.prompt: Why was Lena's wider expectation understandable?

options.text: The ticket included mobile by default.
options.feedback: Mobile was explicitly excluded.

options.text: Omar's handover omitted the word desktop.
options.feedback: 'Export is ready' sounded broader than the agreed scope.

options.text: QA tested Nia's phone.
options.feedback: QA tested the desktop flow.

questions.prompt: What is still important to learn from Lena or Nia?

options.text: Whether the desktop ticket was ever created.
options.feedback: P-248 and its QA result are already documented.

options.text: Whether a mobile date was promised in P-248.
options.feedback: The record explicitly says no mobile date has been agreed.

options.text: Which report Nia needs to export from her phone.
options.feedback: That use case can inform a separate mobile request and its priority.

questions.prompt: What should Omar avoid promising in his reply?

options.text: A clear explanation of desktop scope.
options.feedback: The scope is documented and should be explained.

options.text: That mobile export will ship next week.
options.feedback: There is no agreed mobile delivery date.

options.text: A check of the desktop flow.
options.feedback: Omar can reasonably offer to verify that flow again.

task.prompt: Reply to Lena as Omar. Distinguish completed desktop work from the unmet mobile need, own the ambiguous handover, and propose a useful client update without promising a mobile delivery date.
criteria: Recognise why Lena inferred wider coverage
Propose a next step for Nia's use case

model.subject: Re: Brookline can't find Export
model.body:
Hi Lena,

P-248 marked Done covers CSV export from the desktop Reports page. QA passed that flow on Thursday. That is the work the team marked complete. Mobile was outside the ticket, so the missing button in Nia's screenshot does not show whether the desktop flow is working today.

I can see why my handover note, 'Export is ready', suggested wider coverage. I should have said 'desktop CSV export', and I'm sorry that caused confusion during your call. I'll check the desktop flow again today and document Nia's mobile use case as a separate request. Could you confirm which report she needs to export from her phone? We can then agree its priority and explain the current scope clearly at tomorrow's check-in. We should not offer a mobile delivery date until one has been agreed.

Omar

title: Friday doesn't work
teaser: One short reply to a remote-work request sounds like a ban on an entire team's policy.
misunderstanding: A Friday duty was the constraint, but Alex's terse reply sounded like a broad policy refusal.

email.subject: Sara's Friday request
email.body:
Hi Alex,

Sara says her request to work remotely on Friday was declined. She understood your reply to mean that the new two-day remote policy is not available to her team. Can you clarify the reason and what options she has? I'd like to resolve the confusion before Monday's team meeting.

Priya

document.title: Remote-work policy · rota excerpt
document.intro: The policy and message record provide the facts. No one has checked coverage yet.

facts.text: The team may work remotely up to two days each week when assigned on-site sessions have coverage. The policy has not been suspended.
Sara is named as the in-person host for Friday's new-starter welcome, 09:00–11:00.
Sara asked Alex to work remotely on Friday.
Alex replied only, 'Friday won't work this week.' He did not explain the rota or discuss alternatives.
Nobody has checked whether another trained host can cover the welcome.

questions.prompt: What was the specific constraint on Friday?

options.text: A company-wide ban on remote work.
options.feedback: The policy remains available.

options.text: Sara's performance had been questioned.
options.feedback: The documents say nothing about performance.

options.text: Sara was assigned to host an on-site welcome.
options.feedback: The rota assigns her the Friday 09:00–11:00 session.

questions.prompt: Why did Sara infer that the policy was unavailable?

options.text: The policy had been suspended.
options.feedback: The policy has not been suspended.

options.text: Alex's brief reply gave no reason or alternative.
options.feedback: Without the rota context, 'Friday won't work' could sound like a broader refusal.

options.text: Priya had already declined the request.
options.feedback: The record does not say Priya declined anything.

questions.prompt: What remains unknown before Alex can offer a Friday arrangement?

options.text: Whether another trained host can cover the welcome.
options.feedback: Coverage has not been checked yet.

options.text: Whether Sara asked to work remotely.
options.feedback: Her Wednesday request is recorded.

options.text: Whether the policy allows remote days.
options.feedback: The policy allows up to two with coverage.

questions.prompt: Which reply best resolves the misunderstanding without making an unsupported promise?

options.text: Tell Priya the policy does not apply to this team.
options.feedback: That contradicts the policy.

options.text: Promise Sara can work remotely this Friday.
options.feedback: Coverage is still unknown, so that promise is premature.

options.text: Explain the rota, own the unclear reply, and check coverage with Sara.
options.feedback: That clarifies the reason and leaves room for a real option.

task.prompt: Reply to Priya as Alex. Explain the specific Friday duty, take responsibility for your unclear reply to Sara, avoid commenting on performance or promising unconfirmed coverage, and propose a clear update before Monday's meeting.
criteria: Distinguish the Friday duty from the team policy

model.subject: Re: Sara's Friday request
model.body:
Hi Priya,

The remote-work policy is still available to our team. My reply to Sara was about this Friday's rota, not a general restriction: she is listed as the on-site host for the new-starter welcome from 9 to 11. I wrote only 'Friday won't work this week' and did not explain that distinction or discuss options. I can understand why she read it as a broader refusal, and I should have been clearer.

I have not yet checked whether another trained colleague could cover the welcome, so I cannot say that Friday remote work is impossible. I'll speak with Sara today, explain the duty and ask what arrangement would work for her. Then I'll check coverage and update you both with a clear decision before Monday's meeting. Thanks for flagging the misunderstanding.

Alex
